verdicts.summary: Lean uses a different formula here. The identity half matches exactly; the quantitative lower bound does not appear. Lean's `hid` (ConeAlgebra.lean:124), multiplied out with P_c = p·c, J_c = p·j and p = p_{s,1}, is the paper's identity cleared of denominators: 2(P_c−v)² − (v−2)J_c² = p²G − 4cvp + 2v², i.e. the paper's left side equals G − 4cv/p + 2v²/p² after dividing by p² (same constants, signs and exponents; Lean keeps the p² factor rather than dividing). What Lean then establishes is only strict positivity: from the hypothesis hscale : 4cv < p·(2c² − (v−2)j²) it gets 0 < p·(p·G − 4cv) (line 122) and adds 2v² ≥ 0. It does not produce the uniform bound ≥ γ_K/2, because its threshold branch is 4cv/d < p rather than the paper's 8B_K/γ_K ≤ p (the factor 2 of eq-p031-9). The surrounding result is still proved — only positivity of this expression is needed for v < coneBound via `true_cone_iff` — so the paper's formula as written, with its γ_K/2 margin, is not what was checked; a weaker bound that suffices was.
